 'Confidence in the referee' published at 15:10 GMT 15:10 GMT 
 FT: Leeds 1-0 Tottenham 
 Tottenham Hotspur 
 Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi to TNT Sports : "We deserved to lose the game in the second half and didn't play like we can. It's a journey for us, because we can learn from this game. I am sorry for the performance in the second half - we didn't play like a top team. We didn't have the right character and physicality in the second half."
 On a booking for Pedro Porro compared to Jayden Bogle's tackle on Mathys Tel: "Pedro Porro's was a duel and an incredible yellow card. The first situation of Mathys Tel I didn't see, I can't say nothing."
 On if the referee should have gone to the monitor: "No. I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to the monitor. If they didn't take the right decision I don't know. We have to keep the eyes on the performance where can improve."

 'Bogle is a butterfly' published at 15:07 GMT 15:07 GMT 
 FT: Leeds 1-0 Tottenham 
 Leeds United 
 Leeds boss Daniel Farke to TNT Sports: "We were pushing to win this game and were relentless. We showed great spirit, commitment and unity. It was a fully deserved win."
 On Jayden Bogle's foul on Mathys Tel: "I haven't watched it back. I have heard there were several doubtful situations. A possible hand ball. I just know that Jayden Bogle out of any bad intention. It looked like a coming together. 
 "It's very unlucky outcome that Mathys is injured and we wish him all the best and he can recover quickly. The last thing Jayden Bogle is a nasty player. He's possibly the softest player in the whole league. I always call him my butterfly, and I can guarantee it was never out of bad intention."

 Solid defence getting Gunners through published at 14:57 GMT 14:57 GMT 
 Arsenal v Hull (15:00 GMT) 
 Sophie Brown 
BBC Sport 
 Arsenal may not be quite firing yet in attack – just 14 goals in their nine league games – but they look solid in defence, with their five goals conceded the fewest in the top flight.
 They have the lowest xG conceded (7.24), have faced the fewest shots on target (24) and have had clean sheets in their past three league games.
 The determination they showed at Anfield reflects the fact that they have won all six of the league matches in which they have taken the lead this season.
 Mikel Arteta's sides have developed a habit of this over his years in the top flight, with the Spaniard behind only Sir Alex Ferguson, Pep Guardiola and Jose Mourinho in this category.

 King earns England call up published at 14:54 GMT 14:54 GMT 
 Fulham v Newcastle (15:00 GMT) 
 A big week for Fulham's Josh King, who was called up to Thomas Tuchel's England squad this week for their upcoming Nations League matches against Spain and Croatia.
 The Cottagers seem to be starting to find their feet under Alvaro Arbeloa and King has been at the forefront of that.
 King has recorded more touches in the opposition box this season than any other player in the top flight (57) while of all players to have had 400+ touches this term, King has also had the highest share in the opposition box (13% - 57/438).
 The 19-year-old has bagged two goals and assist this season too.
 Tuchel said: "He is just a fantastic character. He gives us a bit of flexibility.
 "We decided to nominate 22 outfield players for flexibility in training and he is the extra player in training, if you will.
 "He is an exciting player, a versatile player."

 Fulham finding their feet? published at 14:52 GMT 14:52 GMT 
 Fulham v Newcastle (15:00 GMT) 
 Sophie Brown 
BBC Sport 
 It was a sticky start to the season for Fulham but there are signs that they are settling into the more expansive style of play brought in by new head coach Alvaro Arbeloa.
 After picking up just two points in their first six Premier League matches of the season, Fulham have now taken seven points from their past three.
 They conceded 10 goals in those first six games, but just one in the past three.
 Against Aston Villa last weekend, Fulham had almost double the number of touches in the opposition box and completed over 100 more passes than their opponents, and Arbeloa said after the match that "we are a team that want to play in the opposite half with the ball, creating chances."
 Fulham are currently below Newcastle in the table but given the respective levels of form of the two sides. it would be no surprise to see that reversed on Saturday.

 'This game feels big for Jaissle' published at 14:50 GMT 14:50 GMT 
 Fulham v Newcastle (15:00 GMT) 
 What are Newcastle? What type of team are they? I am not sure and that's why their manager, Matthias Jaissle, is getting a bit of stick from Magpies fans.
 That's what is different with today's Premier League compared with my playing days, because we see it all the time now - even a new manager comes under pressure if they have a couple of bad results.
 Newcastle have lost three of their past four league games and, in this day and age, that's enough for people to say the wheels are coming off.
 That's why this game feels big for Jaissle. Win and the Magpies head into the international break on a positive note. Lose it, however, and stand by for a lot of moaning and grumbling from their fans over the next couple of weeks.
 That's what I think will happen, too. Fulham's results have picked up and so have their performances. They are at home here, and I am expecting them to be too slick and too well organised for Newcastle.
 Sutton's prediction: 2-1

 Arsenal's title credentials published at 14:46 GMT 14:46 GMT 
 Arsenal v Hull (15:00 GMT) 
 Sophie Brown 
BBC Sport 
 Arsenal's rare win at Anfield last weekend made it eight wins from their opening nine league matches of the season and sent a message of gritty intent to their Premier League rivals.
 It even had football statisticians Opta speculating on the Gunners winning the title by a record margin, an accolade currently held by Manchester City, who finished 19 points clear in 2017-18.
 While that may be a bit premature, Arsenal's total of 24 points after nine games is the most by a team at this stage of a Premier League season since Mikel Arteta's side also had 24 in 2022-23. But of course they did not win the title that year.
 Only in 2004-05 and 2007-08 (both 25 points) have Arsenal ever had more at this stage of a Premier League campaign. They are two points better off after nine games of this campaign than last season, when they won the title.

 'Jaissle has changed personnel but it's the same tactics' published at 14:44 GMT 14:44 GMT 
 Fulham v Newcastle (15:00 GMT) 
 John Anderson 
Former Newcastle defender on BBC Radio Newcastle 
 Steur came on against Everton the other night, was just positive, wanted to pass the ball forward, wanted to get it to the front players. Whether he and Nico Gonzalez can play together, I don’t know. 
 Jaissle is keeping to the same formula. What’s the old saying? If you keep doing the same thing, you keep getting the same result. Yes, he’s changed the personnel but it’s the same tactics. He says he wants to see our style. I don’t know what our style is. I don’t know what our style of play is at all. 
 Livramento, Miley and Fernandez-Pardo back on the bench is positive but it’s all about the starting eleven. The performance today has to be so much better than the two games against Everton. The win is the most important thing.

 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Noah Okafor scored in Leeds' last Premier League win in September
 By Keifer MacDonald BBC Sport journalist Substitute Noah Okafor scored the only goal of the game as Leeds United defeated Tottenham Hotspur to earn their first Premier League win since September. 
 Switzerland striker Okafor combined with fellow substitute Harry Wilson 11 minutes from time to smash the ball home less than two minutes after his introduction at Elland Road.
 His second goal of the season was enough to earn Leeds three points for the first time in six matches, while simultaneously ending Tottenham's three-game winning streak.
 Leeds, though, were arguably fortunate to still have 11 players on the pitch by the time Okafor broke the deadlock late on, following a controversial end to the first half.
 Tottenham manager Roberto de Zerbi was left incensed by Jayden Bogle escaping punishment for a reckless challenge on Mathys Tel, with tempers flaring just after the half-hour mark.
 Following a VAR check that lasted more than four minutes, referee John Brooks opted against sending off the Leeds defender, who ultimately escaped without a booking.
 De Zerbi's anger was compounded when Tel was subsequently forced off injured and replaced by Dominic Solanke.
 Substitute Solanke made his introduction count five minutes into the second half when he was in the right place at the right time to clear Dominic Calvert-Lewin's header off the line from a corner.
 But the home side continued to push for an opener during a dominant second-half display, with Ao Tanaka and Sean Longstaff also going close before the breakthrough eventually arrived, sending the home supporters into pandemonium.
 After pouncing on a loose ball inside the area and slamming it past Antonin Kinsky, Okafor secured Leeds their first win over Tottenham since May 2021 and lifted them to eighth in the table. Meanwhile, a first defeat in five matches sees Spurs drop to 10th.
 Okafor the difference despite Van Hecke defiance - Leeds v Spurs ratings 
 Published 39 minutes ago 
 Have your say on Leeds' performance 
 What did you make of Tottenham's display? 
 Leeds head into international break with renewed confidence 
 You only had to look at the celebrations inside Elland Road to understand how important this victory was for Leeds.
 Okafor's strike takes Leeds into the top half of the table and will help relieve some of the pressure after a peculiar start to the season as they head into the international break.
 The Yorkshire outfit had yet to fully appease their supporters so far this term, despite losing just two of their first nine Premier League games.
 Their struggles in the final third meant they had won just two matches, with their last victory coming against Newcastle in September, before the visit of a resurgent Tottenham side.
 It will not just be the three points that ease any reservations Leeds supporters may have had about their side during the opening months of the campaign, but also the manner in which they completely dominated and outclassed the north Londoners for much of the second half.
 In truth, it was a scoreline that flattered Tottenham, with several Leeds players going close as they registered 13 shots during a commanding second-half display.
 It is a result that will have the Whites heading into the international break with a spring in their step, while their supporters will already be counting down the days until their team is back in action.
 Toothless Spurs showing will worry De Zerbi 
 It could have been a very different outcome for Spurs had the officiating gone their way in the first half.
 Referee Brooks' decision not to send off Bogle was one that could have handed Tottenham a significant advantage.
 Instead, De Zerbi's side, who lost Tel to injury as a result of the challenge, were left on the back foot and seemingly unable to recover.
 Of course, there was more to Spurs' first defeat in four games than a single decision during a 90-minute match. However, it was a decision that appeared to rile De Zerbi and his players, with the visitors subsequently losing control of the game.
 What will concern the Italian more is the fact that his side failed to create any chances of note during a toothless second-half performance, while Leeds looked capable of scoring almost every time they surged forward.
 After three consecutive Premier League wins, De Zerbi will certainly be disappointed with how easily his side fell to defeat.
